text:
maya: Ran a 12h long-context stress with chat-sim and the KV cache kept growing even after conversations ended. Not pure leak — fragmentation + failed reuse looks likely.
jon: ugh. numbers?
maya: p95 mem for kv_cache on the runner: 5.1GB -> 6.9GB over 12h. heap vs reserved shows big holes.
zoe: any sudden alloc spikes at prefix lengths?
maya: yes, when users hit ~4k token windows. We allocate lots of small variable-length KV entries and then later allocate a few very large blocks for long-attn windows, which splits free lists.
ravi: can you paste profiler snippet?
maya: sure:
```
KV cache stats:
  total_allocated: 7_080_832_128
  total_free: 1_120_345_600
  external_frag_pct: 26.5
  free_runs: 1423
  avg_free_run_bytes: 788
  hot_hits: 1_234_567
  cold_evictions: 24_890
```
jon: 26% external frag is huge. That explains growth without true leak.
serge: what's allocator today? slab-backed with 64/256/1024/4096 classes + large-bins, right?
maya: yes. But the distribution of sizes in chat-sim is multimodal and shifts over time (many small entries then occasional midsize bursts). The slab buddy coalescing doesn't trigger because the large blocks get split and never match adjacency for coalescing.
zoe: ideas: 1) aggressive periodic compaction, 2) tune block size classes to match observed distribution, 3) opportunistic recycling of evicted KVs into small-entry fastpool.
ravi: we tried compaction before and it hit p99 latency because it locks the region. Could we do incremental compaction in small windows?
maya: prototype idea: background "coalescer" that walks free runs during idle CPU ticks, merges adjacent frees without global stop-the-world, and maintains a light-weight deferred free queue to batch frees into size-class-friendly chunks.
jon: +1. Also consider size-class heuristics: add 128B and 2KB classes, and adjust boundaries to avoid frequent split patterns.
serge: what about eviction policy? LRU will kick out items used recently, but token-distance-aware eviction might keep items used within the last N tokens (usefulness heuristic). That reduces churn for long conversations.
zoe: we could tag KV entries with "recent-turns" counter and prefer evicting by (last_used_turn, absolute_size). Might reduce re-allocs.
ravi: benchmark plan?
maya: propose three branches:
  A) compaction daemon (low-overhead incremental)
  B) size-class reshuffle (+ add 128B, +2KB)
  C) eviction-aware reuse where evicted buffers go into small fastpool if size <= 4KB
Let's run each on chat-sim 12h and 24h.
jon: add metric hooks: external_frag_pct, free_runs_count, median_free_run_size, allocation_hotness (reuse within 3 turns). Also track p95/p99 latency.
serge: we should also try adaptive allocation: when allocation pattern is small then big, bias towards allocating from a spare large-bucket to avoid fragmentation instead of splitting. Think pre-splitting heuristics.
maya: right — heuristic: if last 100 allocs avg_size > 1.5x class_size, try allocate next larger class whole.
zoe: tradeoff: wasted internal fragmentation vs reduced external fragmentation. But given 26% external frag, it's worth testing.
infra-bot: deploy queued: maya/kv-coalesce-proto -> staging at 2024-06-04T09:12:00Z (will run perf harness).
ravi: timeline: maya + jon will land compaction prototype WIP by EOD Friday, zoe + serge take size-class tests next week. We'll run A/B across 24hr chat-sim slices.
jon: one more: add a compaction backoff so it only runs when CPU load < 40% and no in-flight cold evictions.
maya: logging plan: short samples every 10m with a quick histogram of free_run sizes to detect bin mismatches.
zoe: sounds good. I'll own dashboards and add alert if external_frag_pct > 20% for > 2 hours.
maya: thanks — I'll post initial perf traces + flamegraphs once staging run completes. :coffee: 
jon: great. if results are promising we can ship heuristic toggle behind feature flag for Dedicated clusters first.
serge: keep an eye on p99 generation latency when compaction runs — don't want visible spikes.
maya: noted. ok I'll update thread with results.
